candidates.claim: B believes the world is improving every year.

proposal_evidence.quote: You honestly believe the world ’ s improving every year ?

auditor.reason: Turn 1's question 'You honestly believe the world's improving every year?' grammatically presupposes that A attributes this belief to B. The word 'honestly' questions sincerity but still presupposes the belief is attributed to B.

candidates.claim: B expressed an opinion that A disagrees with.

proposal_evidence.quote: That ’ s your opinion not mine .

auditor.reason: Turn 9 'That's your opinion not mine' presupposes that B holds/expressed an opinion and that A disagrees with it ('not mine').

candidates.claim: B made a claim that A considers incorrect.

proposal_evidence.quote: I don ’ t think you ’ re right there .

auditor.reason: Turn 3 'I don't think you're right there' presupposes that B made a claim ('you're right there' refers to something B said) and that A considers it incorrect ('I don't think you're right').

proposal_evidence.quote: That ’ s your opinion not mine .
